conditions.function_evidence: The objective of this ground investigation was to use flight data obtained from PSI through NASA’s Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations regulated the dynamics and ultimate fate of already established droplet cool flames

earth_application.value: Advances low-temperature combustion understanding relevant to engine knock, efficiency, and emissions; delivers validated CFD tools transferrable to practical combustors.
earth_application.evidence: Advances low-temperature combustion understanding relevant to engine knock, efficiency, and emissions; delivers validated CFD tools transferrable to practical combustors.

fuel_type.value: n-heptane / air mixture, dimethyl ether (DME) / air mixtures
fuel_type.evidence: (a) spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture, (b) one dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames using an arc-length continuation method and (c) simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

o2_concentration.evidence: a comparative studies of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted

pressure.evidence: simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

sensors_measurements.value: extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution
sensors_measurements.evidence: Obtain new, quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution for the validation of kinetic and radiation models involving cool flames.

test_variables.value: oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection transport processes
test_variables.evidence: The investigation hypothesizes that factors such as oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection transport processes affect the cool flame transition.

conditions.function_evidence: the purpose of this grant was to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to: 1) Develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.

earth_application.value: high-pressure near-limit combustion applications
earth_application.evidence: Since many real engines operate in the 20-40 atm pressure range, therefore, cool flames and warm flames are relevant and important flame regimes for high-pressure near-limit combustion applications.

fuel_type.evidence: Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane; normal and inverse flames; and a broad range of Zst, Tad, and fluent flow rate.

sample_geometry_size.evidence: Steady-state cool diffusion flames on spherical porous burners.
